narrativeBlocks.title: A king's peculiar rule
narrativeBlocks.body: Math, king of Gwynedd, can only hold office while his feet rest in a virgin's lap — a magical condition of rule so specific it reads like law. His nephew Gwydion exploits this to start a war for his brother.

narrativeBlocks.title: The flower-wife
narrativeBlocks.body: Punished for the war, Gwydion's nephew Lleu has a wife made for him by magic — Blodeuwedd, fashioned from oak, broom, and meadowsweet flowers, the most beautiful woman ever made.

narrativeBlocks.title: The wife who was flowers
narrativeBlocks.body: Blodeuwedd loves a stranger and plots her husband's death — he can only be killed under impossible conditions, which she tricks him into demonstrating. She is made of flowers, not flesh — the tale's strange cruelty.

narrativeBlocks.title: Owl in the oak
narrativeBlocks.body: Lleu is not quite killed — he turns into an eagle. Blodeuwedd is punished by being made an owl, shunned by every other bird. Justice in the tale is transformation, not death.

narrativeBlocks.title: The strangest tale of the four
narrativeBlocks.body: The Fourth Branch asks what a person made of flowers owes to human loyalty — and what happens when a created thing chooses for herself. It's the uncanniest of the Mabinogion.
